correctness.rationale: Because the starting structure is already \(K_{m,n}\)-free, any newly created forbidden configuration must use the new line. Such a configuration exists exactly when the chosen neighborhood contains an \(m\)-set already lying on \(n-1\) old lines, which is precisely a hyperedge of the saturation hypergraph. Hence admissible new-line neighborhoods are exactly independent sets. Conversely, replacing each edge of any simple \(m\)-uniform hypergraph by \(n-1\) distinct lines incident exactly with that edge realizes it as the saturation hypergraph without creating \(K_{m,n}\). The hardness gadget adjoining a fixed \((m-2)\)-vertex core to every graph edge has independent-set count \((2^{m-2}-1)2^{|V|}+i(G)\), so one oracle call recovers graph independent-set count. The actual verifier exhaustively checks thousands of small extension instances and gadget identities; the uniform proof does not depend on that enumeration.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete representation theorem for a natural finite extension statistic in a canonical generic-incidence class and transfers the full expressive and exact-counting complexity of hypergraph independent sets. The universality and hardness consequences make it substantially more than a routine single-instance count.

final_claim: For every fixed \(m,n\ge2\), the one-line extension polynomial of a finite \(K_{m,n}\)-free incidence structure is exactly the independence polynomial of its \(m\)-uniform saturation hypergraph; conversely every finite simple \(m\)-uniform independence polynomial occurs, and exact counting at \(z=1\) is #P-complete under polynomial-time metric reductions.
limitations: The result concerns finite models of the universal \(K_{m,n}\)-free theory and a single new line, not complete types in the model companion.
The parameters \(m,n\) are fixed; no approximation-complexity claim is made.
